SRJ Consulting & Services Firm News — May 2026

SRJ Consulting Is Transitioning Fully to AI Advisory

SRJ Consulting Is Transitioning Fully to AI Advisory

Effective immediately, SRJ Consulting & Services LLC operates exclusively as an AI advisory practice. The firm will no longer accept new accounting, bookkeeping, payroll, or QuickBooks engagements.

This is a strategic transition, not an expansion. The firm is now built around a single question that most leadership teams are facing whether they realize it or not: AI is already inside the organization, but who is governing it?

The real questions executives are now asking

For most organizations, AI is no longer a future planning topic. Employees are using AI tools without approval. Vendor platforms are quietly adding AI features. Reporting systems are recommending outputs that influence decisions. Automation is touching workflows that were never reviewed for AI exposure.

The result is a new class of operational question that traditional risk frameworks were not designed to answer:

  • Who is using AI advisory inside the organization, and under what authority
  • What data is being exposed, and to which third parties
  • Which decisions are being materially influenced by AI, and whether accountability is clear
  • Where AI is creating measurable value, and where it is creating cost, confusion, or risk
  • How leadership governs AI without slowing the business down

SRJ Consulting & Services is now built specifically to answer these questions.

Nine service lines, two operating pillars

Engagements are organized into two pillars. Pillar I covers the business-side discipline of AI adoption. Pillar II covers the security and exposure dimension. Each pillar contains specific service lines, scoped independently and engaged based on situation.

Pillar I, AI Business Services™

  • AI Business Enablement Audit™ — diagnostic foundation, evaluating where AI is being used, what it costs fully loaded, and whether it produces measurable outcomes
  • AI Readiness & Performance Assessment™ — forward-looking evaluation of capability to scale AI responsibly
  • AI Risk & Governance Review™ — governance structure for AI risk at the data, decision, and vendor layers
  • AI Efficiency & Process Optimization™ — operational improvement for processes ready to absorb AI

Pillar II, AI Risk Governance & Security™

  • AI IT Security Audit™ — technical evaluation of how AI expands existing security exposure
  • AI IT Security Implementation & Strategy™ — remediation, hardening, and control framework development

The work is operator-led. No software sales, no vendor partnerships, no implementation revenue. The advisory is the product.

What changed and why

My background spans three decades in technology, cybersecurity, infrastructure, risk, operations, and leadership at firms including Citi, Intel, McAfee, and Optiv. That experience now aligns directly with what business leaders actually need from AI advisory work.

Most organizations don’t need another software pitch. They need operating judgment. They need someone who can look across business process, risk, leadership accountability, information flow, security exposure, vendor dependency, and measurable outcomes, then tell them whether AI is making the business stronger or simply adding another layer of complexity. That is where the firm now focuses.

Who this work is for

The firm’s AI advisory services are structured for organizations where leadership is accountable for AI outcomes. The clearest fit is mid-market through enterprise leadership teams whose firms are large enough that AI cannot be ignored but not large enough to maintain a Chief AI Officer or in-house AI governance function. Engagements typically involve executive sponsors, board or audit committee visibility, and a defined operating question that needs answered with structure rather than enthusiasm.

Schedule an AI consultation

If your organization is using AI advisory, considering AI, concerned about AI risk, or unsure whether AI is producing measurable value, the next step is a thirty-minute conversation. No deck. No pitch. A structured discussion about where the organization currently stands and what the right next step looks like.

Schedule a Free AI Consultation →

pages.h1: SRJ Consulting & Services Now Live, With a Free Resource Library for Executives Running AI
pages.main:
SRJ Consulting & Services Firm News — May 2026

SRJ Consulting & Services Now Live, With a Free Resource Library for Executives Running AI

SRJ Consulting & Services LLC came online today at srjconsultingservices.com. The new resource hub at srjconsultingservices.com/books opens with free templates, worksheets, and framework graphics for executives who need to bring AI under management. No email required. No registration. The same artifacts used in active client engagements, made available for any executive who wants to evaluate their own AI operating discipline before talking to anyone.

Most companies are losing 15 to 30 percent of their AI spend to tools no one approved, subscriptions no one tracks, and embedded features no one opted into. The cost shows up in budgets where reporting was never designed to look. By the time leadership asks where the money went, the audit trail does not exist. SRJ Consulting & Services LLC was built to give executives the operating discipline to fix that.

The Unmanaged AI Problem

Inside the mid-market business, AI does not arrive through a single executive decision. It arrives in fragments. An employee starts using a chat tool for drafting. A finance team enables AI features in Excel. A vendor pushes an update that activates AI capabilities no one reviewed. Marketing pays for a tool that nobody else knows about. Customer service runs a chatbot trial that never officially ended.

None of it is governed the way the same business governs finance, hiring, or compliance. The accumulated cost is real. The accumulated risk is real. The opportunity cost of running AI as scattered tools instead of a managed business function is the real exposure.

The fix is not more technology. The fix is operational discipline.

What SRJ Consulting & Services Is Built For

The new SRJ Consulting & Services website is built for executives who need to bring AI under management without first hiring an AI team. The site is organized around how operating decisions actually get made. Where to start. What to evaluate first. How to govern what is already in place. Which resources are open for internal use before any consultant is called in.

SRJ Consulting & Services works with owners, presidents, CFOs, and COOs at organizations from 20 to 1,000 employees. Engagements are senior-led, operator-led, and designed for businesses without dedicated AI teams or unlimited consulting budgets. That same operating posture shapes the public site. The templates, the framework, the worksheets, and the graphics library are all open. The pages do operator work, not marketing work.

What Is Free at srjconsultingservices.com/books

The new resource hub consolidates every published artifact from the firm into one location. No gates. No forms. Open access. The same templates running inside active engagements, posted without modification, because executives evaluating their own operating discipline should not have to negotiate for the tools to do it.

Currently live:

The full template and worksheet set. The AI Tool Inventory for surfacing every AI tool, subscription, and embedded feature currently running. The Real Cost of AI worksheet for translating fragmented spend into a single number leadership can act on. The Risk Categorization framework for sorting exposure by severity rather than vendor. The Vendor Governance template for closing the gap between procurement and operations. The Operational Health Check for evaluating whether AI is supporting the business or stretching it. The Decision Accountability Framework for naming, by function and by quarter, who owns what. All formatted as ready-to-edit Excel and Word files.

The Chapter Graphics Library. Every figure, diagram, and framework graphic from the SRJ operating discipline framework, available as a downloadable PNG file. Use them in board decks, internal memos, leadership offsites, or team training. No permission requests. No attribution friction.

Where to Start

If your leadership team cannot name, by function and by quarter, who is accountable for AI, what it costs, and what happens when it goes wrong, the resources at srjconsultingservices.com/books are where I would start. Read the framework. Run the templates against your own business. See what shows up.

For executives whose organizations need a senior review from SRJ Consulting & Services, or a working session to walk through the framework in your specific context, call +1 (415) 413-7772 or schedule a free AI consultation.

pages.main:
AI Strategy — May 2026

Why We Are Not an AI Tool Vendor And Why That Matters to Your Leadership Team

Artificial intelligence is exploding across every industry.

New platforms promise automation.
Dashboards promise insight.
Chatbots promise productivity.

And vendors promise transformation.

But here is the uncomfortable truth:

Most AI initiatives fail because they start with an AI tool vendor rather than with leadership.

At SRJ Consulting & Services LLC, we are not an AI tool vendor. And that is intentional.

Tools Do Not Solve Leadership Gaps

Software can automate workflows.

It cannot:

• Align executive incentives
• Create governance structures
• Define accountability
• Harden identity controls
• Measure ROI across departments
• Correct cultural resistance
• Prevent performative adoption

– Ensure executive incentives are aligned – Establish governance frameworks – Clarify accountability – Strengthen identity verification processes – Assess ROI throughout various departments – Address cultural resistance – Avoid superficial adoption

When organizations buy from an AI tool vendor without structured oversight, three things happen:

  1. AI use becomes fragmented
  2. Risk expands silently
  3. ROI becomes anecdotal

AI does not fail because of bad technology.
It fails because of unstructured adoption.

AI Is Now a Leadership Criterion

In today’s market, AI fluency is becoming part of executive credibility.

Boards are asking:

• Is leadership AI-enabled
• Is AI adoption measurable
• Is AI governed
• Is exposure controlled
• Is AI improving the margin

This is no longer an IT question.
It is a governance question.

Buying another platform does not answer that.

The Difference Between Automation and Oversight

AI vendors focus on:

• Workflow acceleration
• Evidence scoring
• Dashboards
• Feature sets

We focus on:

• Executive alignment
• Governance frameworks
• Risk quantification
• Identity and access exposure
• Infrastructure vulnerability
• Measurable performance impact

They improve processes.

We align leadership.

The Risk of Performative Adoption

When AI usage becomes tied to incentives, promotions, or market signaling, a dangerous dynamic can emerge:

• Log-ins instead of integration
• Experimentation without controls
• Adoption without accountability
• Scaling without security

Without structure, AI increases risk as quickly as it increases capability.

That is where our advisory work begins.

AI Business Services™

Structured Value Creation

We ensure AI adoption is:

• Business-first
• Measurable
• Governed
• Aligned to financial outcomes

This includes:

• AI Business Enablement Audit™
• AI Readiness & Performance Assessment
• AI Governance & Compliance Review
• AI Efficiency & Process Optimization

Our objective is clarity and performance, not tool deployment.

AI Risk Governance & Security™

Structured Risk Containment

AI expands attack surfaces.

It accelerates phishing, impersonation, exploit cycles, and identity infiltration.

Our AI IT Security Audit™ and AI IT Security Implementation & Strategy™ programs focus on:

• Technical exposure
• Identity hardening
• API and integration risk
• Governance frameworks
• Executive-level visibility

We quantify exposure before it becomes a financial event.

Why Tool-Agnostic Matters

When advisory firms are tied to software, recommendations can become product-driven.

We remain tool-agnostic.

That means:

• No commission bias
• No platform dependency
• No upsell pressure
• No vendor lock-in incentives

We advise leadership — not software.

AI Is Infrastructure Now

Artificial intelligence is no longer a feature.
It is infrastructure.

Infrastructure demands:

• Oversight
• Governance
• Controls
• Accountability
• Measurement

That is executive territory.

Not app-store territory.

The Bottom Line

If you are searching for:

“Best AI tool”
“Top AI platform”
“Free AI software”

We are not the right fit.

We are not an AI tool vendor, and we will not become one.

If you are asking:

• Is AI structured correctly in our organization
• Is leadership aligned
• Are we exposed at the infrastructure level
• Is adoption measurable and governed
• Are we increasing margin or increasing risk

Then we should talk.

Executive Consultation

AI is already in your business.
The question is whether it is structured, governed, and secure.

Call (415) 413-7772 or schedule a confidential AI consultation:
Schedule a Fee AI Consultation!

forms_note: Contact and client-upload forms post to the Worker endpoints /api/contact and /api/upload. They replace WPForms blocks that posted to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php, which does not exist on the static site: WPForms' noscript fallback was all that rendered, so visitors saw 'Please enable JavaScript in your browser to complete this form' and no form. The A2P 10DLC SMS disclosure and the PHI notice are carried verbatim from production.
gap_page_note: Five category archives ship without a meta description on production. Architecture package gate 16 requires these be written rather than copied empty, and logged as improvements. desc_source marks each one. The three governance gap pages (china-ai-regulation, global-ai-laws, sources) are handled in srj-content/governance/. The remaining two of the package's ten are locations.kml, a file, and /resources/ai-glossary/, which 301s to a page that already has one.
